narrative.en:
The skaldic-reception file holds the court-poetry's mythic citations. The shield-poems: the myth-panels (Bragi's Ragnarsdrapa and Thjodolfr's Haustlong - the records norse-thor-fishing-serpent and norse-haustlong-skaldic: the corpus's oldest narrative-myth witnesses), the poets' ekphrasis as the courts' myth-books.

The genealogy-lays: the god-descent sung for jarls (Eyvindr's Háleygjatal - the record norse-jarls-foundation-stories' title-deeds; the mythic genealogy as court-commission), the cult-verses: the halls' images described (Úlfr Uggason's Húsdrápa: Baldr's funeral, Thor's fishing and Heimdall's? - the hall's painted walls skaldically narrated - the skald as the interior's guide-book), and the temple-verses: the exploits sung (Eysteinn's fishing-stanzas; Eilifr's Geirrod-lay - the records' skaldic witnesses).

The kenning-census completes the catalog: the myths as working vocabulary ('the? - mead? - 'of? - Odin? - 'for? - poetry; 'Ymir's? - 'blood? - 'for? - the? - sea; 'Freya's? - tears? - 'for? - gold? - - each kenning a myth-citation, the record norse-kenning-origin's grammar evidenced across the whole corpus). The record's cultural functions are the reception-catalog doctrine (the myth corpus's oldest continuous witness: the skaldic corpus documenting the myths' circulation century by century) and the citation-economy doctrine (each poem a myth-citation's receipt: the myths' court-currency documented). In the atlas, the record anchors the skaldic-reception family: each a tradition's court-poetry citation-file; the Norse one is distinctive in the kenning-economy.

For the database, this node indexes the skaldic-records already in the corpus: here the citation-census.

The catalog's chronology completes the register: the citations dated century by century (the 9th-century shield-poems' myths, the 10th-century genealogy-lays, the 11th-century cult-verses, the 12th-century lausavisur) - the skaldic-reception file as a timeline of the myth corpus's court-currency: which myths the courts still knew, and when, documented poem by poem. And the meter's discipline completes it: the dróttkvætt constraints guaranteeing the citations' antiquity (the myths embedded in verse-forms that could not be casually invented) - the reception-file's dating-method documented.

The file's lost-layer problem completes the register: the skaldic corpus's losses documented (the poems known only through quotations - Snorri's Edda preserving verses whose long poems are gone), so the reception-file's witnesses are fragments of a destroyed library: the citation-census compiled from survivals, the myth-corpus's court-currency known only where the quotations kept it. And the database's own use completes it: the skaldic citations as the corpus's dating-instrument (the myths' antiquity argued from the verse's attestation) - the reception-file working as the myth database's chronometer.

 The file’s Havamal-citation completes it: the wisdom-lay’s own verses cited in the court-tradition (the guest-craft maxims quoted in the sagas’ halls) - the reception-file’s reach documented from the shield-poems to the proverb-book.

summary.en: The myth-corpus's picture-file: the Altuna stone (Thor's fishing carved with the hammer raised: 'the? - 'one? - 'stone? - 'with? - 'the? - 'whole? - scene), the Gotland picture-stones (Tjängvide's rider on the eight-legged horse - Odin's Sleipnir-ride carved; Ardre's hall-scenes), the runestone panels (the Sigurd-scenes of the record norse-sigurd-rune-stones; the Gosforth cross - the record norse-gosforth-cross), the stave-church portals (the Hylestad cycle), and the manuscript-drawings (the 17th-century Edda-paper MSS' illustrated myth-sheets: the myths drawn for learned readers). The record is the picture-register file.

narrative.en:
The picture-register file holds the myth corpus's carved and drawn register. The Altuna stone: the fishing carved (the god, the ox-head bait, the hammer raised - the record norse-thor-fishing-serpent's scene in stone: 'the? - 'whole? - 'fishing? - 'on? - 'one? - face? - - the iconographic case-study). The Gotland picture-stones: the rider on the eight-legged horse (Tjängvide's mounted figure above the hall-scene - Odin's Sleipnir-ride carved for the dead: the ride-to-Valhalla as picture), and Ardre's scenes (the hall-images and the smith-scene - the Ardre VIII stone's Völundr-panels: the record norse-volund-smith's iconographic twin).

The runestone panels and portals: the Sigurd-scenes and the Ragnarök-cross (the records' carved material - the dragon-slayer and the doom on Christian stone), and the manuscript-drawings: the 17th-century myth-sheets (the Edda-paper MSS' illustrated pages: the myths drawn for the learned collectors - the corpus's picture-reception's late register). The record's cultural functions are the picture-register doctrine (the myths documented in image independent of the manuscripts: the iconography as a parallel witness-stream) and the image-context doctrine (each carving in its context: the memorial, the church-door, the collector's page - the pictures' functions dated by their settings). In the atlas, the record anchors the picture-register family: each a tradition's myth-image file; the Norse one spans stone to parchment.

For the database, this node complements the carved-records: here the pictures' file.

The file's identifications-method completes the register: the picture-record's evidentiary care documented (each carving's reading argued from the attributes: the eight legs, the ox-head, the heart - the iconography's grammar reconstructed attribute by attribute), so the picture-file's method is the database's own: inference from documented detail, with uncertainties labeled. And the manuscript-drawings' provenance completes it: the 17th-century myth-sheets' collectors (the learned Icelanders drawing the gods for the antiquarian market) - the picture-register's late layer documented as scholarship's first illustrated mythology.

The file's geographic-spread completes the register: the images' distribution documented (the Gotlandic picture-stones, the Swedish runestones, the English crosses, the Norwegian portals - one iconography across the Norse world's coasts), so the picture-file's reach is the diaspora's: the myths carved wherever the Norse settled, the image-register mapping the tradition's territory. And the dating-method completes it: the carvings' styles sequenced (the ornament-chronology used to date the myth-scenes) - the picture-register's chronology documented by style, the images' order argued from their borders.

 The file’s Gosforth-junction completes it: the English cross’s panels joining the Swedish stones in one register - the picture-file’s geography spanning the whole Norse world, the images dated and compared across the sea.

title.en: The Learned Romances: Trójumanna saga, Breta sögur and Merlínússpá
title.zh: 博學傳奇：《特洛伊薩迦》《布列塔尼人之書》與《梅林預言詩》

region.en: The learned Iceland of the 13th century (symbolic pin at Pingvellir)
region.zh: 13世紀的博學冰島（象徵性定位於辛格維利爾）

texts.period: riddara-sogur and learned translations c. 1200-1250 (Haukr Erlendsson's circle); Merlinuspa by Gunnlaugr Leifsson, c. 1200

source.work: Trojumanna saga; Breta sogur (with Merlinuspa); Hauksbok's compilation; the Latin romances' Norse translations

summary.en: The late-medieval compendia's file: Trójumanna saga (the Trojan War's Norse retelling: the classical epic translated into saga-prose), Breta sögur (Geoffrey's Historia regum Britanniae in Norse: the British kings' book), and Merlínússpá (Gunnlaugr Leifsson's verse translation of Merlin's prophecies in eddic metre - 'the? - 'prophecies? - 'sung? - 'in? - 'the? - old? - measure? - - the French prophecy translated into the North's prophetic form). The record is the learned-reception file: the imported prophecies read in the native genre.
summary.zh: 晚期中世紀彙編檔案：《特洛伊薩迦》（以薩迦散文轉述特洛伊戰爭——古典史詩的北歐化）、《布列塔尼人之書》（傑弗里的《不列顛諸王史》之諾斯譯本），以及《梅林預言詩》（貢勞格·萊夫松以埃達韻律譯寫的梅林預言——「以古體韻律吟唱的預言」：法蘭西預言被譯入北方的預言文體）。此記錄是博學接受檔案：外來預言以本土文體閱讀。

narrative.en:
The learned-reception file holds the imported-myth register. Trójumanna saga: the classical epic in saga-prose (the Trojan War translated for the Norse courts - the Dares-Phrygius tradition's saga-form: the classical heroes made saga-kings), and Breta sögur: the British book in Norse (Geoffrey's Historia translated - the British kings' and Arthur's material entering the north's bookshelf).

Merlínússpá completes the file: the prophecies translated into the native genre (Gunnlaugr Leifsson's verse rendering of the Prophetiae Merlini - 'the? - 'prophecies? - 'sung? - 'in? - 'the? - old? - measure? - - the imported prophecy wearing the eddic form: the sibyl-tradition (the record norse-voluspa-sibyl) meeting Merlin - the reception's mirror: the North's prophecy-genre used to carry the imported doom). The record's cultural functions are the learned-translation doctrine (the romances translated into saga-prose: the North's bookshelf internationalized) and the genre-mirror doctrine (the imported prophecy carried in the native prophetic metre - the corpus's reception-datum: how the North read foreign dooms through its own). In the atlas, the record anchors the learned-romance family: each a tradition's imported-myth register; the Norse one is distinctive in the metre.

For the database, this node documents the late-medieval compendia: the reception-file's learned layer.

The file's translation-method completes the register: the romances' Norse renderings documented (the saga-prose's domestication of the classical and British materials: the heroes renamed, the geography relocated, the Christian frame added), so the learned-reception file documents the import's adaptation: how the North's translators naturalized the foreign dooms and dynasties. And the corpus's afterlife completes it: the rímur-tradition's continuation (the later verse-cycles reworking the imported material) - the learned layer's reception documented through the post-medieval centuries.

The file's verse-craft completes the register: Merlínússpá's metre documented (the eddic fornyrðislag carrying the French prophecies - the translation's formal choices itemized), so the learned-reception file documents the import at the level of metre: the foreign doom fitted to the native form, stanza by stanza. And the Hauksbok-context completes it: the compilation's program (Haukr Erlendsson's law-book and the learned texts bound together - the imports shelved beside the native law) - the learned layer's library documented as one household's canon.

 The file’s prophecy-genre junction completes it: the Voluspa-sibyl and Merlin read as the North’s two prophet-voices - the imported seer naturalized beside the native one, the learned-reception file’s genre-mirror closed.

 The file's Haukr-Erlendsson signature completes it: the compilation)s compiler documented (the law-man)s hand in the learned layer - the imports) patron named), the learned-reception file)s library traced to its owner.

title.en: The Ritual of Cursing: Runes, Poles and the Law

summary.en: The cursing-ritual's legal file: the pole-curse's procedure (the record norse-egill-nithing-pole: hazel, horse-head, formula, landward turn - the full technology), the law's clauses (níð and scolding as offences: the curse-word's legal weight - 'the? - 'word? - 'of? - shame? - 'that? - 'unmans? - - the chargeable insult), the rune-curse formulas (the runestones' threat-clauses - the record norse-bjorketorp-curse's descent-line), and the taboo's persistence (the curse's folk-afterlife in the post-conversion countryside). The record is the curse-law file.
summary.zh: 詛咒儀式法律檔案：木樁詛咒的完整程序（榛木、馬頭、套語、轉向內陸——見埃吉爾記錄）、法律條款（níð與辱罵為罪行——「使人失格的羞辱之言」可被控告）、如尼詛咒套語（如尼石的威脅條款——布約克托普石之後裔），以及禁忌延續（皈依後鄉野中詛咒的民俗後續）。此記錄是詛咒法律檔案。

narrative.en:
The curse-law file holds the cursing-ritual's full procedure and its legal frame. The pole-curse's technology (norse-egill-nithing-pole holds the scene): the procedure's parts documented (the hazel-pole, the horse-head, the juridical formula, the landward turn - the curse filed as a lawsuit with the land itself). The law's clauses: the curse-word's legal weight ('níð? - 'and? - scolding? - 'chargeable? - offences? - 'the? - 'insult? - 'that? - 'unmans? - - the Grágás and Gulathing clauses: the spoken curse prosecuted as violence, the corpus's speech-law), and the rune-curse formulas: the runestones' threat-clauses (the records' descent-line from the Blekinge stones' doctrine to the Glavendrup outlaw-curse).

The taboo's persistence completes the file: the curse's folk-afterlife (the post-conversion countryside's cursing-stones and nith-poles documented in the later folklore - the record norse-rune-stone-legends-local's register), the ritual surviving its law. The record's cultural functions are the curse-as-law doctrine (the curse prosecuted: the north's speech-crimes documented - the corpus's clearest speech-jurisprudence) and the ritual-procedure doctrine (the curse's technology itemized: the corpus's most complete magic-instruction). In the atlas, the record anchors the curse-law family: each a tradition's formalized cursing; the Norse one is distinctive in the pole's procedure.

For the database, this node complements the pole-record and the rune-curse-records: here the legal frame.

The file's evidence-grammar completes the register: the curse's prosecution documented in the cases (the insult-lawsuits of the sagas: the níð charged, defended and compensated - the speech-crimes' court-procedure itemized), so the curse-law file documents not just the rules but their operation: the curse-word's price in the courts, the insult's compensation paid like a wound. And the runic-law's junction completes it: the carved curses' legal standing debated (the runestones' threats as law or as magic - the file's open question, the carved word's jurisdiction ambiguous by design).

The file's gendered-register completes the law: the curse's social reach documented (the women's cursing documented beside the men's poles - the saga-women's insult-craft as the household's weapon), so the curse-law file's subjects are both sexes: the formal pole-curse for the landowner, the spoken curse for the kitchen - the corpus's speech-crimes documented across the household. And the Christianity-clause completes it: the curse's criminalization completed (the converted law's escalating penalties: fines, then outlawry, then burning) - the ritual's arc ending in the stake, the file's chronology documented to its end.

 The file's runestone-pole junction completes it: the carved and the planted curses' shared grammar documented (the formula, the naming, the direction - the two technologies one speech-act in two media), the curse-law's procedure certified by its own consistency.

narrative.en:
The verse-wergild file holds the head-ransom's episode. The capture: Egill shipwrecked at the enemy's court ('the? - 'poet? - 'at? - 'the? - mercy? - of? - 'the? - king? - 'whose? - land-spirits? - 'he? - 'had? - cursed? - - the record norse-egill-nithing-pole's curse returning to its author: the poet caught by the king he had driven out).

The night's composition and the recitation: the head-ransom composed in the dark (the dróttkvætt masterpiece paid for the head - 'the? - 'poem? - 'made? - 'in? - 'one? - night? - 'the? - - the corpus's most famous composition-legend: the death-sentence converted to art in a night's work), the recitation at the king's court (the poem 'that? - 'turned? - 'the? - death? - - the ransom accepted: the king's judgment converted to payment - the corpus's clearest case of poetry as currency), and the compensation-case: the later arbitration (Egill's claim against the crown settled at the law-rock: the wergild's institutional form - the poet's family-claim argued by the poet himself, the record norse-ulf-outlaw-boundary's law-world in the poet's own case).

The record's cultural functions are the verse-wergild doctrine (the poet's head priced in meter - the corpus's currency-theory at its purest: art as legal payment) and the composition-legend doctrine (the night-made masterpiece as the skaldic ethos: the craft's worth proven under sentence). In the atlas, the record anchors the verse-wergild family: each a tradition's poet-ransoms; the Norse one is distinctive in the meter.

For the database, this node complements the pole-record and the outlaw-record: here the payment-file.

The file's meter-craft completes the register: the head-ransom's dróttkvætt documented (the poem's internal rhymes and alliteration woven under death-pressure - the composition-legend's technical claim examined: whether the masterwork was made in one night or polished after), so the verse-wergild file documents both the legend and its skepticism: the poem's price debated as the corpus's own crux. And the compensation-case's aftermath completes it: Egill's later settlement with the crown (the wergild's final form: the arbitration's payment and the poet's peace) - the verse-payment's institutional closure documented.

The file's geography completes the register: the head-ransom's road documented (the shipwreck's shore, the court at York, the return by the northern route - the poet's journey mapped), so the verse-wergild file's episode has a map: the ransom performed in the enemy's capital, the payment carried home by sea. And the poem's survival completes it: the Hofudlausn's transmission (the stanzas preserved in the saga and the skaldic books - the ransom's art outliving the ransom) - the payment's instrument still readable, the corpus's currency documented in its own surviving coin.

narrative.en:
The dark-rune file holds the corpus's cursing-formulas. The catalog's dark entries: Hávamál's offensive songs (the hate-song, the storm-song, the banishing-rune - the record norse-poetic-edda-havamal's magic-list's dark side), and Sigrdrífumál's protective-versus-offensive pair (the ale-runes against witchcraft; the speech-runes as courtroom armor - the record norse-sigrdrifa-song).

Skirnir's threats: the wooing-curse in full (the limbs' withering, the terror's eyes, the giant below the corpse-gate - the record norse-freyr-gerd-skirnir: the corpus's most complete curse-text, the threats itemized stanza by stanza), and the runestones' threat-clauses: the descent-line (the Blekinge stones' guard-formula to the Glavendrup outlaw-curse - the records' stone-register). The saga curse-episodes complete the file: the singing-bones and the sorcerers' logs (the Grettir-saga's rune-log - the record norse-grettir-saga; the saga-world's performed curses - the magic documented in narrative action).

The record's cultural functions are the dark-rune taxonomy (the cursing-formulas classified: spoken, carved, sung - the corpus's magic-grammar) and the weaponized-rune doctrine (the runes as instruments of coercion: the alphabet's legal and magical registers united). In the atlas, the record anchors the dark-rune family: each a tradition's cursing-formula file; the Norse one is distinctive in the wooing-curse.

For the database, this node complements the rune-records: here the dark register.

The file's transmission-note completes the register: the curse-formulas' continuity documented (the skaldic curses' echoes in the later verse and the folk-charms - the dark-rune register's afterlife through the conversion), so the evil-runes file documents the formulas' persistence: the alphabet's coercive power surviving its pagan frame, the curses recited in Christian-era farm-magic. And the ethics-of-magic completes it: the corpus's own judgment on the dark-runes (the Hávamál's warning-clauses against the misuse: 'better? - 'not? - to? - ask? - than? - too? - much? - to? - offer) - the magic-system's self-limitation documented as doctrine.

The file's carved-versus-spoken distinction completes the register: the formulas' media documented (the runestones' carved threats permanent; the sung curses' performance transitory; the carved curse-boards? - the? - 'lead? - 'and? - 'wood? - 'charms? - 'of? - 'the? - archaeology) - the dark-rune register's media-theory: permanence chosen for property-curses, voice for personal ones. And the Skirnir-scene's staging completes it: the wooing-curse performed with the drawn? - the? - 'the? - 'staff? - 'and? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'horse? - 'the? - ritual-props documented - the curse-text's staging preserved in the poem's own directions.

 The file's Havamal-coda completes it: the magic-songs’ closing warnings (the songs not to be sung for pay, the runes not to be cut for harm’s hire) - the dark-rune register’s ethics documented as the tradition’s own exit-clause.

narrative.en:
The trial-file holds the saga-courts' witchcraft-cases. Katla's case: the shape-magic caught by procedure (the witch's invisible seal-hide stripped off in the mob's ducking-bath? - 'the? - 'hide? - 'stripped? - 'in? - 'the? - 'the? - - the corpus's most famous shape-magic trial: the invisible witch caught by the legally-prescribed bath, the shape-shift defeated by due process). Geirrid's duel-trial: the magic demonstrated as evidence (the walking-through-the-wall shown in the legal duel's? - 'the? - 'demonstration? - 'at? - the? - door? - - the wizard's proof staged for the court).

Thuridr's log: the witch as the law's hired instrument (the rune-carved driftwood floated to the island that killed Grettir - the record norse-grettir-saga: the sorcery commissioned by the landholders, the corpus's witch-as-employee), and the law's fjölkyngi-clauses: the sorcery-outlawry (the Grágás clauses: the magic-worker as an outlawable offence - the record norse-seidr-gullveig-expanded's law-register).

The record's cultural functions are the magic-trial doctrine (the saga-courts prosecuting the visible magic: shape-magic tested by procedure - the corpus's trial-method documented) and the witch-as-instrument doctrine (the sorcerer hired: the magic-labor-market the sagas document). In the atlas, the record anchors the magic-trial family: each a tradition's courts testing magic; the Norse one is distinctive in the shape-procedure.

For the database, this node complements the seiðr-record and the curse-records: here the trials' file.

The file's procedure-grammar completes the register: the trials' evidentiary machinery documented (the oath-helpers, the demonstration-witnesses, the depositions of the neighbors - the saga-courts' magic-cases run by ordinary procedure), so the trial-file documents the corpus's refusal of exceptional courts: the witch tried like any litigant, the magic-case heard as a property-dispute. And the convictions' aftermath completes it: the outlawries and compensations imposed (the sorcerers' sentences documented in the settlements) - the trials' outcomes logged, the corpus's magic-crimes priced.

The file's pre-Christian register completes the law: the seiðr-trials' older layer (the saga-world's memory of the pre-conversion practice - the volvas tolerated as specialists before the statutes), so the trial-file's chronology runs from tolerated craft to capital crime: the magic-law's arc documented in the sagas' own memory. And the gender-grammar completes it: the trials' subjects overwhelmingly female (the male sorcerers' cases the exceptions) - the corpus's magic-crimes gendered as its seiðr-taboo, the trials' demography documented as doctrine.

 The file’s saga-junction completes it: the trial-episodes’ literary placement (the witch-trials staged at the feud-narratives’ pivots - the magic-case as plot-engine), the corpus’s trials documented as drama as well as procedure.
